entry: [[Transition metal]] with atomic number 25 (symbol Mn). Hard, brittle and silvery, manganese is usually found in [[Mineral|minerals]] combined with [[Iron|iron]]; it was first isolated in 1774 by Swedish chemist Johan Gottlieb Gahn. Over 90% of global manganese consumption goes into [[Steelmaking|steelmaking]] as a deoxidizer and desulfurizer, improving strength, hardness and wear resistance in [[Stainless steel|stainless steels]]. Manganese compounds are also used in batteries, fertilizers, pigments and water treatment. It is an essential trace element, a cofactor for enzymes involved in metabolism, antioxidant defense and bone formation. In plants it forms part of the oxygen-evolving complex that splits water in [[Photosynthesis|photosynthesis]]. Excess exposure can cause neurotoxicity resembling [[Parkinson's disease]].

Tropical stone fruit of the tree *Mangifera indica*. It originated between the northeastern part of the [[Indian subcontinent]] and [[Myanmar]] and has been cultivated in South and Southeast Asia since ancient times. Several hundred cultivars vary in size, shape, sweetness, and skin and flesh color. Mango is the national fruit of [[India]], [[Pakistan]] and the [[Philippines]], and the mango tree is the national tree of [[Bangladesh]]. Trees grow 30–40 metres tall, and some specimens still fruit after 300 years. A 100-gram serving of raw mango provides about 60 [[Calorie|calories]] and 1 gram of [[Protein (nutrient)|protein]].

Tropical evergreen tree with an edible fruit, *Garcinia mangostana*. Native to the [[Malay Peninsula]] and [[Borneo]], it has been cultivated across tropical Asia since ancient times and grows 6 to 25 metres tall. The fruit has an inedible purplish rind enclosing sweet, tangy, fragrant white segments. Polyphenols in the rind, including xanthones and [[Tannin|tannins]], make immature fruit astringent and deter pests.

[[Shrub]] or tree growing mainly in coastal saline or [[Brackish water|brackish water]]. Mangroves occur in tropical and subtropical coastal areas, mostly between latitudes 30° N and 30° S, and tolerate salt through a complex salt filtration system and specialized root systems. Their forests stabilize shorelines and protect nearby areas from [[Tsunami|tsunamis]] and extreme weather, and they are effective at [[Carbon|carbon]] sequestration and storage. In 2025 the global area was estimated at 15.9 million hectares, with Indonesia holding the largest extent at 3.40 million ha. Human activity continues to cause losses, with a global annual deforestation rate estimated at 0.16%, and per-country rates as high as 0.70%. Restoration success may depend on engagement with local stakeholders.

Borough of [[New York City]] and [[County (United States)|county]] in [[New York (state)|New York State]] (pop., 2020: 1,694,250). Smallest of the city's five boroughs by area and the most densely populated, it serves as its economic and administrative center. Dutch colonists set up a trading post on Manhattan Island in 1624, which was named New Amsterdam in 1626. New York, based in Lower Manhattan, was the U.S. capital from 1785 to 1790. The [[Statue of Liberty]] in New York Harbor greeted millions of immigrants. The borough houses [[Wall Street]], the [[New York Stock Exchange]] and [[Nasdaq]].

Allied nuclear weapons program of [[World War II]]. Led by the United States with the United Kingdom and Canada, the project employed nearly 130,000 people at its peak and cost nearly US$2 billion. Major General Leslie Groves directed it from 1942 to 1946, while [[J. Robert Oppenheimer]] directed the Los Alamos Laboratory in [[New Mexico]], where the bombs were designed. [[Uranium|Enriched uranium]] was produced in Tennessee, and [[Plutonium|plutonium]] was made in the world's first industrial-scale nuclear reactors at Hanford in Washington. The first nuclear detonation, the [[Trinity (nuclear test)|Trinity test]], took place in New Mexico on July 16, 1945. Bombs were used against [[Hiroshima]] and [[Nagasaki]] in August 1945, hastening the end of the Pacific War. The project was succeeded by the United States Atomic Energy Commission in January 1947.

Mood disorder marked by abnormally elevated mood, hyperactivity and risky behavior. Symptoms include irritable or euphoric mood, flight of ideas, decreased need for sleep and hyperactivity. In severe episodes of [[Bipolar disorder|bipolar I disorder]], [[Delusion|delusions]] or [[Hallucination|hallucinations]] may occur, and [[Psychosis|psychosis]] appears in 57% of manic episodes compared with 13% of depressive ones. In a mixed state, with concurrent depressive symptoms, the risk of [[Suicide|suicide]] is greater. More than 5% of people have experienced mania or hypomania to some degree.

Dualistic [[Religion|religion]] founded in the third century AD by the Iranian prophet Mani in the [[Sasanian Empire]]. Its cosmology describes a struggle between a good world of light and an evil material world of darkness, through which light is gradually returned to the divine. Most forms of the faith regarded Mani as the final prophet after [[Zoroaster]], [[The Buddha|Buddha]] and [[Jesus]]. Missionaries spread it through Aramaic-speaking regions, the Mediterranean and the Middle East, and it was briefly the main rival to early [[Christianity]]. Persecution by the Roman state and the Christian church largely removed it from Roman lands by the end of the sixth century. The [[Abbasid Caliphate]] repressed it in the 10th century, and it was the official religion of the [[Uyghur Khaganate]] until its collapse in 840.

19th-century U.S. belief in westward expansion across [[North America]]. Rooted in American exceptionalism, it held that the nation had a divinely ordained mission to spread republican government. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrats]] used it to justify the 1846 Oregon boundary dispute, the 1845 annexation of Texas as a slave state and the [[Mexican–American War]]. Opponents, including [[Abraham Lincoln]] and [[Ulysses S. Grant]], rejected the concept and opposed the war. It is also associated with settler expansion onto Indigenous lands. After the [[American Civil War]], the U.S. acquired Alaska in 1867, and in the 1890s [[William McKinley]] annexed Hawaii, the Philippines, Puerto Rico, Guam and American Samoa.

[[Topological space]] locally resembling [[Euclidean space]] near each point. An *n*-dimensional manifold has a neighborhood around each point that is homeomorphic to an open subset of *n*-dimensional Euclidean space. One-dimensional manifolds include lines and circles, and two-dimensional manifolds, called surfaces, include the [[Sphere|sphere]], the [[Torus|torus]] and the Klein bottle. Manifolds are central to geometry and modern physics: differentiable manifolds allow calculus, a Riemannian metric allows distances and angles to be measured, and four-dimensional Lorentzian manifolds model spacetime in [[General relativity|general relativity]]. Studying them requires knowledge of [[Calculus|calculus]] and [[Topology|topology]].

Capital of the [[Philippines]] (pop., 2024: 1,902,590), on the eastern shore of Manila Bay in [[Luzon]]. A Tagalog-fortified polity called Maynila existed on the site by 1258. On June 24, 1571, after the defeat of its last indigenous ruler, Rajah Sulayman, Miguel López de Legazpi began building the walled fortification of Intramuros. Manila was the capital of the Spanish East Indies, administered from [[Mexico City]] within the Viceroyalty of [[New Spain]], and its galleon trade linked Asia with the [[Americas]]. Under American occupation it became the country's first chartered city in 1901. Manila is the world's second most natural disaster-exposed capital after [[Tokyo]]. [[Typhoon|Typhoons]] and poor drainage cause recurrent flooding. It forms the core of [[Metro Manila]].

State in [[Northeast India|northeastern India]], with Imphal as its capital. Mostly hilly, it is home to the Meitei people, who make up around 53% of the population and live mainly in the Imphal Valley. Manipur was a princely state under the [[British Raj]] and merged with India in 1949, an agreement many Meitei feel violated their self-determination. A long-running insurgency against Indian rule has been accompanied by ethnic violence, which displaced over 60,000 people after May 2023. The state is credited with introducing [[Polo]] to Europeans.

Province of Canada at the country's longitudinal center. Its capital and largest city is [[Winnipeg]]. The landscape ranges from [[Arctic]] [[Tundra|tundra]] and the coast of [[Hudson Bay]] in the north to boreal forest, lakes and [[Prairie|prairie]] in the south. Under the [[Hudson's Bay Company]], Rupert's Land, which included the present province, was administered from 1670 until 1869. Armed resistance led by [[Louis Riel]] preceded Manitoba's entry into Confederation as the fifth province on July 15, 1870. French holds official legislative and judicial status alongside English.

Indian economist and politician, prime minister of India from 2004 to 2014. A member of the [[Indian National Congress]], he was the first and remains the only Sikh prime minister. Born in Gah, in present-day Pakistan, he earned a doctorate in economics at the [[University of Oxford]] and worked for the [[United Nations]] from 1966 to 1969. As finance minister from 1991 he carried out structural reforms that liberalized India's economy. In 2004 [[Sonia Gandhi]] unexpectedly gave up the prime ministership to him. His first ministry carried out key legislation, including the Right to Information Act. His coalition was returned with an increased mandate in 2009, but its second term was marked by political scandals. In 2009 [[BRICS]] was established with India as a founding member.

Style in European art, emerging around 1520 and lasting in Italy until about the end of the 16th century. Mannerists reacted against the ideals of the High [[Renaissance]], exaggerating the proportion and balance of [[Leonardo da Vinci]], [[Raphael]] and [[Michelangelo]] to create asymmetrical or unnaturally elegant compositions. The term derives from the Italian *maniera*, meaning style or manner. Its definition remains debated, and some scholars apply it to late 16th- and 17th-century poetry and music. The [[Baroque]] style largely replaced it in Italy, while in Spain, [[El Greco]] adapted it in his late works.

Filipino boxer and former politician. Nicknamed PacMan, he is widely regarded as one of the greatest boxers of all time and is the only eight-division world champion in boxing history. He served as a senator of the [[Philippines]] from 2016 to 2022 and lost the 2022 presidential election. [[Forbes]] ranked him the second-highest-paid athlete in the world in 2012 and 2015. In 2024 [[ESPN]] ranked him the greatest Asian athlete of the 21st century. He has faced criticism for his social conservatism, including opposition to [[Same-sex marriage|same-sex marriage]] on religious grounds.

Large ray of the [[Genus|genus]] *Mobula*. *M. birostris* is the largest, reaching 7 metres (23 feet) across, and *M. alfredi*, at 5.5 metres, is smaller. Manta rays have triangular pectoral fins, horn-shaped cephalic fins and large, forward-facing mouths, and they filter-feed on [[Plankton|plankton]] as they swim. They live in warm temperate, subtropical and tropical waters and have one of the highest brain-to-body ratios of any fish. *M. birostris* and *M. alfredi* are listed as vulnerable by the International Union for Conservation of Nature. Threats include [[Pollution|pollution]], entanglement in fishing nets and harvesting of gill plates, which are traded internationally. Their slow reproductive rate worsens these pressures.

Order of [[Insect|insects]] containing over 2,400 species, including the praying mantises. Mantises are found worldwide in temperate and tropical habitats. They have triangular heads on flexible necks and greatly enlarged forelegs for catching prey, and their upright posture with folded forearms resembles prayer. Most are ambush predators, and they normally live for about a year. Their closest relatives are [[Termite|termites]] and [[Cockroach|cockroaches]]. Females sometimes practice sexual cannibalism. Early civilizations, including [[Ancient Greece]], [[Ancient Egypt]] and [[Assyria]], believed mantises had supernatural powers, and they are among the insects most commonly kept as [[Pet|pets]].

Carnivorous marine [[Crustacean|crustacean]] of the order Stomatopoda, with more than 520 living species. They are among the most important predators in many shallow tropical and subtropical habitats, though they are poorly understood because many species spend most of their lives in burrows. Their raptorial appendages are either spearing types, which impale prey on spiny structures, or smashing types, which strike with a heavily mineralized [[Club (weapon)|club]]. Their [[Compound eye|compound eyes]] detect [[Ultraviolet|ultraviolet]] and [[Polarization (waves)|polarized]] light. Their name comes from forelimbs that resemble those of [[Mantis|mantises]].

Sacred utterance, syllable or phrase, often repeated in meditation. The word derives from [[Sanskrit]] roots meaning mind and instrument, so a mantra is understood as a mental tool to focus thought. Its earliest mentions appear in the [[Vedas]] and the Avesta of ancient Iran, and practitioners believe mantras have religious or spiritual power. The seed syllable [[Om]] is a mantra in various Indian religions, and in [[Hinduism]] it is believed to be the first sound. A common practice is japa, the meditative repetition of a mantra, often with prayer beads. Mantras are central to [[Buddhism]], [[Jainism]], [[Zoroastrianism]] and [[Sikhism]], although their use and meaning vary among traditions.

[[Byzantine Empire|Byzantine]] emperor from 1143 to 1180. His reign saw the last flowering of the Komnenian restoration, when the empire regained military and economic power. He allied with [[Pope]] Adrian IV, unsuccessfully invaded the [[Kingdom of Sicily]], and established a Byzantine protectorate over the [[Crusader states]]. He joined a combined invasion of [[Egypt]] with the [[Kingdom of Jerusalem]] and placed Hungary under Byzantine hegemony. The campaign that ended at Myriokephalon against the Seljuk Turks was the last unsuccessful effort to recover inner [[Anatolia]]. Some historians argue that his power reflected the Komnenos dynasty rather than his own achievements.

German professional footballer and goalkeeper for Bayern Munich. He is known for a sweeper-keeper style that takes him well outside his penalty area. The IFFHS named him best goalkeeper of the 2011–2020 decade. After joining Bayern Munich from Schalke 04 in 2011, he won multiple [[Bundesliga]] titles and two [[UEFA Champions League]] titles, in 2013 and 2020. He won the [[FIFA World Cup]] with Germany in 2014 and holds the record for most World Cup appearances by a goalkeeper. He has been named IFFHS World's Best Goalkeeper five times, a joint record.

Breed of [[Cat|domestic cat]] originating on the [[Isle of Man]]. A dominant [[Mutation|mutation]] in a [[Gene|gene]] shortens or removes the tail, and the breed is best known for being entirely tailless, with elongated hind legs and a rounded head. Manx were prized as skilled hunters of [[Rodent|rodents]] and were a preferred ship's cat breed. The mutation can cause Manx syndrome, a form of spina bifida that may lead to spinal deformities, incontinence and [[Arthritis|arthritis]].

Interpretation of [[Quantum mechanics|quantum mechanics]] holding that all possible measurement outcomes occur in different worlds. Hugh Everett proposed it in 1957 as the relative state formulation, and Bryce DeWitt popularized the name many-worlds in the 1970s. Apparent wave function collapse is explained by decoherence, which produces branches that correspond to different outcomes. It is intended to resolve paradoxes such as [[Schrödinger's cat]], and it is considered mainstream, though critics object to the proliferation of unobservable worlds.

Variety of [[Marxism–Leninism]] developed by [[Mao Zedong]] for China, officially called Mao Zedong Thought. It stressed a united front of progressive forces leading revolution in pre-industrial societies and a mobilized peasant base. From the 1950s until [[Deng Xiaoping]]'s reform and opening up in the late 1970s, it was the ideology of the [[Chinese Communist Party]]. The [[Great Leap Forward]] led to famine in 1959–62, and the [[Cultural Revolution]] brought factional strife and persecution. After the Sino-Soviet split, the Chinese Communist Party and the [[Communist Party of the Soviet Union]] each claimed to be the sole heir of [[Joseph Stalin]].
